subject: Learning Methods
title: Visual Models as Teaching Tools
description: A quick, practical guide to Visual Models as Teaching Tools.

hook.text: Watson and Crick built a physical 3D model of DNA and won a Nobel Prize. The model revealed structure words couldn't.

buildup.text: Visual and spatial models externalize abstract relationships. They make invisible connections visible and manipulable.

discovery.text: Drawing a diagram or concept map while teaching forces you to decide how ideas connect.

twist.text: The process of creating the model teaches more than the model itself. Building is understanding. Viewing is just seeing.

climax.text: Sketch a diagram of any concept you are studying. Each arrow and label is a claim about how the system works.

punchline.text: Draw the relationships. Building the model is the learning.

quiz.question: Why does building a visual model teach more than just viewing one?
options: Drawing uses motor memory which is stronger
Creating the model forces decisions about how ideas connect
Visual models contain more information than text
